title: Rehearsal (balanced client): Patient booking app · BrightSmile Dental Group

client.label: Client (simulated)
client.job: Plays the client from their own email: budget, deadline, priorities, a hidden ceiling.
client.summary: Round 4: walk_away (Time-and-materials estimate is not capped; Required reminders, visit/balance view, and card payments are excluded)

negotiator.label: Empower Negotiator
negotiator.job: Chooses model, scope, discount and concessions; never types a price.

referee.label: Referee
referee.job: Code: prices every offer with the Deal Desk calculator and enforces discount and margin rules.

coach.label: Sales Coach
coach.job: Reads the rehearsal, including the client's private thoughts, and writes the call plan.
coach.summary: Reopen with a complete, capped fixed-price MVP proposal—not another discount on the incomplete Phase 1—and validate scope and pre-April delivery before promising either.

data.message: The full-scope estimate is well beyond the range we discussed, and an April 23 go-live misses our early-April deadline. The earlier first phase is more promising, but it needs to explicitly include SMS and email reminders, visit and balance visibility, and card payments—not just booking and account access. Could you rework this as a fixed-price, HIPAA-compliant first phase covering all of those priorities, with Dentrix sync and a committed go-live before early April?
objections: Full-scope estimate exceeds budget range
Full-scope go-live misses busy-season deadline
First-phase scope omits explicit reminders and balance/card payments
Time-and-materials estimate leaves cost risk
data.private_thoughts: I can stretch above the stated budget if the must-haves are all protected and delivery is reliable, but not anywhere near the current $157,400 full-scope estimate without board approval. The 2027-02-13 phase date is workable only if the missing patient communications and payment functionality are included; request a credible fixed-price phase and clear HIPAA/Dentrix assumptions.

trace.text: Round 0: negotiating (Full-scope estimate exceeds budget range; Full-scope go-live misses busy-season deadline)

data.message: A fixed-price first phase can meet the early-April timing, but the requested reminders, visit and balance visibility, and card payments are not all included in the current Phase 1 definition, so I can’t responsibly promise them under that estimate. I recommend we start with a paid discovery to resolve the open integration and payment questions, then lock the prioritized MVP scope, fixed price, and schedule; we’ll defer any remaining features to a later phase. If you can approve discovery promptly and keep the MVP focused on the agreed must-haves, we can target a go-live ahead of early April.
concessions: Paid discovery before confirming the expanded MVP scope and fixed-price commitment
data.internal_reasoning: The listed Phase 1 price exceeds the client’s stated budget ceiling and excludes features they now require, so discounting to force the expanded scope would be unsound. Fixed-price speaks to their certainty request, while paid discovery and explicit scope prioritization protect feasibility; no unsupported delivery guarantee is made.

data.message: The fixed price and February go-live are helpful, but this Phase 1 still omits reminders, visit and balance visibility, and card payments—those are core requirements, not optional follow-ons. Please rework the fixed-price scope to include those, along with HIPAA-compliant handling and Dentrix sync, and confirm the go-live remains before early April. At this price, I’d also need a meaningful reduction or a clearly defined first phase that protects those must-haves.
objections: Core patient reminders and visit/balance/payment features are excluded
Price remains above stated budget
Need explicit HIPAA scope and assurances
data.private_thoughts: Could stretch above stated budget if all must-haves are explicitly covered at a fixed price and delivery is credibly before early April. The current offer is near the private ceiling but omits too much; ask for a concession and certainty. A complete scoped offer around $80-92k could close without board escalation.

trace.text: Round 1: negotiating (Core patient reminders and visit/balance/payment features are excluded; Price remains above stated budget)

data.message: I hear that reminders, visit and balance visibility, and card payments are must-haves, but they are outside the currently estimated Phase 1, so I won’t imply they’re covered or promise a fixed delivery date before sizing them. I propose the defined Phase 1 on a time-and-materials basis, targeting the February go-live, with a paid discovery up front to answer the open Dentrix, payment, and compliance questions and then re-estimate the expanded MVP. If you can approve discovery promptly, confirm those features as the prioritized MVP, and agree to manage additions through change control, we’ll bring back a fixed scope and schedule for your approval before implementation.
concessions: Paid discovery before committing the expanded MVP scope, price, and delivery schedule
Target February go-live applies to the currently defined Phase 1 only; expanded requirements require validation and re-estimation
data.internal_reasoning: The client's requested extras are outside the available Phase 1 definition; a price cut cannot responsibly promise them or guarantee the schedule. Offer the estimated Phase 1 at T&M with paid discovery and explicit scope/change-control trade for prompt approval, preserving healthy margin and avoiding a false fixed-price commitment.

data.message: I can’t approve an $86,000 time-and-materials estimate for a Phase 1 that still excludes reminders, visit and balance visibility, and card payments; those are essential for us. Please come back with a fixed-price first phase that includes those capabilities, HIPAA-compliant handling, and Dentrix synchronization, with a committed go-live before early April. If that scope can’t fit, I’m open to a tightly defined alternative that still covers all of those must-haves, but I need the cost and delivery risk capped before we proceed.
objections: Current Phase 1 omits core patient features
Time-and-materials estimate lacks a cost cap
Need firm pre-April go-live commitment
data.private_thoughts: I’m not willing to sign this as offered. The $86k price is already above my stated budget, and it buys only partial scope with cost uncertainty. I can stretch toward my private limit if they cap the price, cover all six must-haves including reminders, balance/visit views and card payments, and protect the early-April launch; otherwise a smaller phase is acceptable only if it still includes those must-haves.

trace.text: Round 2: negotiating (Current Phase 1 omits core patient features; Time-and-materials estimate lacks a cost cap)

data.message: I understand that the omitted capabilities are essential, and I won’t represent them as included in the current Phase 1 estimate. The responsible next step is a short, paid discovery focused on reminders, visit and balance visibility, card payments, Dentrix, and HIPAA controls; we’ll then return a capped fixed-price MVP scope and schedule for approval, with any nonessential items deferred. If you’ll authorize discovery promptly, confirm these as the prioritized requirements, and use change control for additions, we can validate whether a pre-April launch is achievable before committing to implementation.
concessions: Paid discovery before implementation to resolve integration, payment, and compliance questions; re-estimate and confirm scope, capped price, and schedule for approval.
data.internal_reasoning: The priced Phase 1 excludes the client's core requirements, so discounting or claiming it meets the ask would be misleading; the full scope also misses the deadline. T&M Phase 1 is the priced, timely foundation, but make implementation conditional on paid discovery, client prioritization, and change control, then only commit to the expanded fixed scope and schedule after sizing.

data.message: I can’t approve this offer: it’s still time-and-materials, and it excludes reminders, visit and balance visibility, and card payments. We’ve been over this several times; please send a capped, fixed-price proposal that includes those capabilities, HIPAA-compliant handling, Dentrix synchronization, and a committed pre-April go-live. If you can’t provide that, we’ll need to move forward with another vendor.
objections: Time-and-materials with uncapped cost risk
Must-have reminders, visit/balance view, and card payments excluded
No fixed commitment for complete scope
data.private_thoughts: I still prefer to close with Empower if the actual must-have MVP is fixed-price and lands before early April. The repeated refusal to scope these core features is wearing down confidence; get a concrete complete offer near the stated budget, potentially stretch modestly for genuine risk protection, but don't accept discovery or the current partial offer.

trace.text: Round 3: negotiating (Time-and-materials with uncapped cost risk; Must-have reminders, visit/balance view, and card payments excluded)

data.message: I understand, and I’m sorry we’ve repeated an offer that doesn’t cover your essentials. I can offer the currently estimated Phase 1 on T&M with a February target, but it excludes reminders, visit and balance visibility, and card payments, so I cannot honestly call it your required capped, fixed-price proposal or commit to a pre-April launch for the expanded scope. If you’re willing to authorize a short paid discovery promptly and use change control, we’ll return a fully scoped, capped proposal for those requirements; otherwise, I understand if you choose another vendor.
concessions: Paid discovery to resolve the added feature, integration, and compliance requirements before implementation; requires prompt authorization and agreement to change control.
data.internal_reasoning: Used the final-round, policy-compliant discount on the only phase that can plausibly fit near the stated budget, rather than discounting an infeasible full scope. The estimate does not include the client's essential added features, so we must state plainly that it cannot satisfy their capped-price and date demands without discovery and re-estimation.

data.message: Thanks, but the 5% discount doesn’t address the core issue: this is still an uncapped time-and-materials Phase 1 that excludes reminders, visit and balance visibility, and card payments. We’ve been clear that those capabilities, HIPAA-compliant handling, and Dentrix synchronization are required, with a committed launch before early April. Please send a capped fixed-price proposal for that scope; otherwise, we’ll proceed with another vendor.
objections: Time-and-materials estimate is not capped
Required reminders, visit/balance view, and card payments are excluded
No commitment for expanded scope before early April
data.private_thoughts: We have repeated the same unmet requirements several times and this latest offer is still not actionable. I could stretch beyond the stated budget if a capped price and meaningful delivery assurances covered every must-have, but I won't keep negotiating against an incomplete T&M estimate. Empower would need to return with the complete fixed-price MVP and credible pre-April commitment to reopen the discussion.

trace.text: Round 4: walk_away (Time-and-materials estimate is not capped; Required reminders, visit/balance view, and card payments are excluded)

data.headline: Reopen with a complete, capped fixed-price MVP proposal—not another discount on the incomplete Phase 1—and validate scope and pre-April delivery before promising either.
likely_objections: The priced Phase 1 repeatedly excluded the client's stated essentials: reminders, visit and balance visibility, and card payments.
T&M left the client exposed to uncapped cost; they explicitly required a capped fixed price.
No credible pre-April commitment was made for the expanded scope, despite it being a core deadline.
The offers did not resolve HIPAA handling assumptions alongside Dentrix synchronization and the added features.
The final 5% discount reduced the price of the wrong scope; it did not address the client's reason for declining.
concession_path: Acknowledge the repeated mismatch and reset around the client's six must-haves: booking, reminders, visit/balance visibility, card payments, HIPAA controls, and Dentrix sync.

Offer paid discovery only as a short, clearly bounded step with defined deliverables: validated requirements, integration/payment assumptions, capped MVP price, and a schedule decision. Ask whether the client will authorize it if it produces that proposal.

After discovery, trade scope sequencing—not unsupported promises: prioritize a tightly defined MVP containing every must-have, and defer nonessential items such as the website or staff scheduling administration.

Present fixed-price risk protection and a pre-April launch commitment only if engineering validates both. If the complete MVP cannot meet the date, offer a transparent alternative schedule rather than implying the current Phase 1 meets the need.
Seek approval for the validated proposal; involve a Director for any discount above 5%, and never exceed the 10% policy maximum.
data.walk_away_point: Do not discount the currently defined Phase 1 or promise its February target as delivery of the expanded MVP. Stop if the client requires a capped price and pre-April guarantee before the added scope, integrations, and schedule are validated, or if the validated complete MVP cannot meet the margin floor; offer a smaller scope only if it still covers every stated must-have.
what_worked: The negotiator correctly avoided claiming that unestimated features were included and did not promise an unvalidated fixed price or launch date.
The proposal recognized that the full-scope offer at $157,400 missed both the client's budget range and early-April target; phased delivery was directionally sound.
what_to_avoid: Do not repeat the same partial $86,000 T&M offer across rounds after the client has repeatedly named the missing capabilities and requested a cap.
Do not use a discount as a substitute for scope alignment. The $81,700 offer remained incomplete and uncapped.
Do not make paid discovery a generic condition without specifying its outputs, duration, decision gate, and how it leads to the requested capped proposal.
Do not cite the inconsistent $142,300 forecast; deal facts list full-scope T&M at $157,400 and fixed at $176,200.
Do not present the listed Phase 1 schedule as confirmed for expanded scope; validate the schedule after resolving open questions.
questions_to_ask: Will you authorize a short discovery if its written output is a must-have MVP scope, capped fixed-price proposal, and validated go-live schedule?
Are reminders, visit and balance visibility, and card payments all required in the first launch, or can any be delivered immediately after launch without compromising your board's objective?
What exactly must be included in HIPAA handling and acceptance, and what Dentrix access, interfaces, or vendor dependencies can BrightSmile provide?
What is the latest acceptable launch date before busy season, and what client-side decisions or approvals can you commit to making promptly?
